articles.title: Allograft Strut Fixation to Humeral Bone: A Biomechanical Comparison of Suture-Tape Cerclage, Wire Cerclage, and Screws.
articles.authors: Saffi M, Fleet CT, Iio R, Gallagher CA, Johnson JA, Athwal GS
articles.population: Cadaveric humeral bone specimens with allograft struts
articles.outcomes: Compressive force, contact area between strut and bone, and strut movement under cyclical loading
articles.take_home: Lag screws and wire loops performed better than suture-tape for holding bone grafts to the upper arm bone during shoulder surgery. Lag screws may be safer because they need less exposure of surrounding tissue during surgery.

articles.title: Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy: A Comprehensive Guide for Shoulder Surgeons.
articles.authors: Gonzalez-Morgado D, Lohre R, Hachem AI, Elhassan B
articles.outcomes: Scapular winging, overhead activity, surgical outcomes of scapulothoracic arthrodesis, complications
articles.take_home: FSHD causes progressive shoulder muscle weakness and scapular winging that can be difficult to diagnose. Surgery to fuse the shoulder blade to the chest wall may help appropriately selected patients, particularly those with severe winging and limited overhead movement but working deltoid muscles.

articles.title: Geographic Distribution of Shoulder Arthroplasty in the United States: A Rural-Urban Analysis.
articles.authors: Calem DB, Mendiratta D, Mehta P, Lingaum S, Katakam A, Murthi AM
articles.study_type: Descriptive epidemiology study analysing national trends in geographic distribution
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons performing shoulder arthroplasty in the United States
articles.sample_size: 974 surgeons in 2013, increasing to 2,649 surgeons in 2024; 533,569 procedures total
articles.outcomes: Geographic distribution of surgeons across urban, large town, small town and rural areas; procedural volume trends; procedures per surgeon by region
articles.take_home: Shoulder arthroplasty procedures have grown threefold since 2013, but surgeons remain heavily concentrated in urban areas with little expansion into rural communities. Revision surgery is performed almost exclusively in urban centres, meaning rural patients may have limited local access to complex shoulder procedures.

articles.title: Single-Shot Versus Continuous Interscalene Blockade in Primary Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials and Observational Studies.
articles.authors: Torrez C, van de Wall BJM, Rippen E, Beeres FJP, Camenzind RS
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials and observational studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anatomic or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 2,639 patients across 7 studies (1,182 single-shot interscalene blocks, 1,457 continuous interscalene catheters)
articles.outcomes: Pain intensity at 24 hours (primary outcome), opioid consumption, length of hospital stay, technical and block-related complications, and procedural costs
articles.take_home: Single-shot nerve blocks worked about as well as continuous catheters for pain control after shoulder replacement surgery at 24 hours, but had far fewer complications and cost much less. Both techniques provided similar pain relief overall, though the type of local anaesthetic used made a small difference.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Arthroscopic Pre-Revision Tissue Biopsy in Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Nguyen CN, Drake JH, Mounajjed MM, Grogan BF, Cotter EJ
articles.study_type: Retrospective case control, diagnostic accuracy study
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic pre-revision tissue biopsy prior to shoulder arthroplasty revision surgery
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value of tissue biopsy for diagnosing periprosthetic joint infection, compared to intraoperative cultures at revision surgery
articles.take_home: Tissue biopsy taken before revision shoulder surgery was not reliable at detecting infection, missing infection in 70% of cases. A negative biopsy result should not be used alone to decide against revision surgery if doctors suspect infection.

articles.title: Heterotopic ossification after complex elbow fracture-dislocations - Mid-term outcome and risk factor analysis.
articles.authors: Jakobi T, Surgeon O, Schnetz M, Surgeon O, Koch DA, Surgeon O, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent surgical treatment for complex elbow fracture-dislocations (terrible triad injuries, Monteggia fractures, coronoid fractures, and transolecranon fracture-dislocations)
articles.outcomes: Incidence and severity of heterotopic ossification (bone growth in soft tissues); range of motion; Mayo Elbow Performance Score; Oxford Elbow Score; Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand score; risk factors for heterotopic ossification
articles.take_home: Heterotopic ossification developed in about one third of patients after complex elbow fracture-dislocation surgery and was associated with reduced elbow movement and poorer functional scores. Male patients, those with terrible triad injuries, and those who had delayed surgery (more than 5 days) were at higher risk of developing this complication.

articles.title: A Comparison of the Agreement of Four AI Models on Surgical Recommendations of MIRCTs Using the ASES Neer Circle Delphi Recommendations as a Baseline.
articles.authors: Vauclin C, Flaig B, Haynes A, Verma A, Lobao M
articles.study_type: Computer modelling study comparing AI language models
articles.population: Massive irreparable rotator cuff tear scenarios
articles.sample_size: 61 clinical scenarios analysed across 4 AI models with 4 different tests each (976 total recommendations)
articles.outcomes: Agreement between AI model surgical recommendations and expert consensus from ASES Delphi study. OpenEvidence achieved highest accuracy at 65.6-68.9% across tests. Accuracy improved with patient age over 70, dynamic instability, and pseudoparesis; decreased with repairable subscapularis.
articles.take_home: AI language models showed only moderate agreement with expert shoulder surgeons on complex rotator cuff tear cases, with the best model correct around two-thirds of the time. These tools might help doctors in under-resourced settings or non-specialists, but cannot yet replace expert clinical judgement.

articles.title: Comprehensive Conservative Treatment and Surgical Management of Elbow Common Flexor Tendon and Common Extensor Tendon Tears, 200 Operative Cases with Average 9 Year Follow-up.
articles.authors: Herman ZJ, Mohr D, Arner JW, Bradley JP
articles.population: Patients with medial or lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow or golfer's elbow) who failed conservative treatment and underwent surgery
articles.sample_size: 200 surgical patients (165 with follow-up data); 548 total patients treated conservatively
articles.outcomes: Resolution of preoperative symptoms (average 94.5%), current daily elbow pain (average 0.4 out of 10), return to work (96%), persistent difficulties with daily activities (4.2%)
articles.take_home: Surgery for elbow tendon tears that do not improve with conservative treatment for about 14 months produces excellent long-term results, with most patients experiencing near-complete symptom relief and returning to work. Patients with hyperlipidaemia, anxiety or depression, or a smoking history are at higher risk of needing surgery if conservative treatment is chosen first.

articles.title: Low-tension rotator cuff repair for retracted tears: Balancing mechanical relaxation and footprint coverage.
articles.authors: Vu DA, Nguyen TT, Pham TN, Vu DN
articles.population: Patients with large, chronic, retracted rotator cuff tears
articles.outcomes: Repair tension, footprint coverage, retear rates, tendon microvascular flow, cuff integrity at 24 months
articles.take_home: For retracted rotator cuff tears, surgeons should balance restoring the full repair footprint against keeping repair tension low, as high tension may increase failure risk and reduce blood flow to the tendon. A tension-aware approach tailored to individual patients may be safer than forcing the tendon to cover the full footprint.

articles.title: Perioperative proton pump inhibitors use and postoperative surgical complications following primary total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Ninness H, Woodland J, Rogalski BL, Eichinger JK, Ponce BA, Friedman RJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total shoulder replacement
articles.outcomes: Aseptic loosening, dislocation, revision surgery, and overall complications at 3 years
articles.take_home: Patients taking proton pump inhibitors around the time of shoulder replacement surgery had higher rates of implant loosening, shoulder dislocation, and need for revision surgery over 3 years compared to those not taking these medications. This suggests proton pump inhibitors may be a risk factor to consider before shoulder replacement.

articles.title: Prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes of patients with coracoid-based pain after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Su F, Fiandeiro M, LaMonaca J, Charlton A, DeMario NJ, Ramsey ML, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 67 patients with coracoid pain and 201 matched controls
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of coracoid pain, risk factors for developing coracoid pain, resolution with non-operative treatment
articles.take_home: Coracoid pain after reverse shoulder replacement is uncommon (occurring in 1% of patients) and usually gets better on its own, with about half of patients experiencing complete symptom relief within 5 months using non-surgical treatments. The condition is more likely in patients with osteoporosis and in those where the surgeon's technique resulted in less space around the coracoid bone.

articles.title: Risk of venous thromboembolism after knee, hip, or shoulder arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study of 476,620 procedures using linked hospital and primary care data.
articles.authors: Swain S, Leith N, Brown S, Wright Drakesmith C, Rees JL, Bankhead C, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee, hip, or shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Venous thromboembolism (blood clots) within six months of surgery
articles.take_home: Blood clots occurred in about 1 to 2 in every 100 patients after joint replacement surgery, with rates declining over time for hip and knee surgery. New NHS guidelines introduced over the study period did not significantly reduce clot rates for knee and hip surgery, though shoulder surgery showed a 9% reduction after the 2018 guidelines.

articles.title: Patient-evaluated functional outcome is systematically different from physician-evaluated outcome after proximal humerus fracture fixation.
articles.authors: Sahu D, Chaubey A, Shah D
articles.population: Patients who underwent locking plate fixation for displaced proximal humerus fractures
articles.sample_size: 74 shoulders in 72 patients (mean age 56 years, 56% male)
articles.outcomes: Constant-Murley score (physician-evaluated) versus shoulder subjective value (patient-evaluated); associations with pain, range of motion, and shoulder strength
articles.take_home: Doctors and patients often disagree about how well the shoulder is working after fracture surgery. Shoulder pain is the main factor linked to patients feeling their outcome is poor, whilst limited movement and weakness alone were not independently associated with poor patient satisfaction.
